name: RoboBench
description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. The benchmark covers diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation, drawing from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection. It introduces an MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation framework for planning that assesses embodied feasibility by simulating whether predicted plans can achieve critical object-state changes under physical and visual constraints.
creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang; State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University; Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence; Institute for Brain and Intelligence, Fudan University; University of Science and Technology Beijing; Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
citeAs: Luo et al. RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801v1 [cs.RO], 20 Oct 2025.
rai:dataCollection: Datasets are built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Instruction comprehension data uses explicit instructions from daily-life scenarios rewritten into implicit forms using LLMs. Perception reasoning data is constructed across robotic-centric, object-centric, scene-centric, and task-centric aspects using real robot data, curated static attributes, GPT-generated functional properties, Gemini-segmented video steps, manual annotations, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Generalized planning data is built from high-quality robotic videos with Gemini-generated structured annotations refined by human annotators. Affordance prediction data is sampled from the planning pool and annotated with static, dynamic, and mobile affordances. Failure analysis data includes execution-level failures collected from RoboMIND and labeled by experts, and planning-level failures synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real-world robotic datasets including RH20T (Fang et al., 2023), Open X-Embodiment (Collaboration et al., 2023), RDT-1B (Liu et al., 2024b), datasets from Liu et al. (2024c), RoboMIND (Wu et al., 2024), AgiBot World (Bu et al., 2025), and others including Lin et al. (2024a), Mu et al. (2023), Yang et al. (2024). In-house collected robotic data was also used. Object attribute data was sourced from Gao et al. (2024).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Explicit task instructions were rewritten into implicit demand-based requests using LLMs. Robot videos were converted into natural language task descriptions using Gemini. Natural language step descriptions were mapped to predefined function sequences. Function arguments were instantiated with specific object references. Planning-level failure data was synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A two-stage quality control process was applied: (1) data filtering during construction using general criteria (image quality, task validity) and task-specific filters (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks); (2) post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators checking linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy was also applied: items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail are manually reviewed and corrected. Frame sequences were extracted from robotic videos as standardized inputs. All perception data was standardized into multiple-choice QA format.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Gemini generated structured annotations for planning tasks including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments), which were then refined by human annotators. Each step was mapped into function templates. For perception tasks: robotic-centric QA used template-based generation with type and view metadata; object-centric combined curated static attributes with GPT-generated functional properties and distractors; scene-centric used Gemini-segmented video steps for temporal grounding plus manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes; task-centric used human-labeled bounding boxes. Affordance annotations (static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, mobile base positions) were created from sampled planning pool frames. Execution-level failure annotations were labeled by experts from RoboMIND data. A directed acyclic graph (DAG) capturing inter-step dependencies was manually annotated for planning evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy was used: items that all models solve correctly are removed (considered too easy), whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction. Human evaluation was conducted on 438 sampled long-horizon planning tasks to validate the automated evaluation metric, with expert annotators assigning holistic scores (0-20) considering skill selection, object identification, and plan executability. Pearson correlation between human scores and automated metrics was computed to assess alignment.
rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence. It aims to advance embodied AI for manipulation in dynamic, unstructured environments, which has broad implications for robotics applications in real-world settings.
rai:dataBiases: Planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which may bias models toward single-arm scenarios. Real-world planning failure data is lacking, requiring synthesis of planning-level failures by perturbation. The benchmark relies heavily on data from specific robotic platforms and datasets, which may not cover all real-world scenarios.
rai:dataLimitations: Existing planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, limiting cross-embodiment evaluation. Real-world planning failure data is unavailable, so planning-level failures are synthesized. The benchmark covers specific embodiment types (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile manipulator, humanoid) and may not generalize to all robotic platforms. Execution-level failure diagnosis is intrinsically difficult, with even human evaluators achieving only 47.30 on this dimension.
rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. The benchmark is designed for evaluating instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis capabilities. It provides a leaderboard and actionable insights for advancing embodied brain development in robotic AI. Not recommended for training due to the majority-vote filtering that removes items all models solve correctly.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators conducted comprehensive quality inspections. Expert annotators (with prior training) assigned holistic scores for human evaluation of planning data.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (for video segmentation, structured annotation generation including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata); GPT (for generating functional properties and distractors for object-centric perception tasks); VLMs and detection models (used in annotation pipeline for various dimensions)
